precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. We do not have that book.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
In 2 Esdras 14 the Lord had Ezra write the books over: “In forty days they wrote two hundred and four books.” The first were to be published openly, “that the worthy and unworthy may read it”, but the seventy last were kept back. The scriptures themselves show that this is true, because they name books we do not have.

Joshua 10:13 is the first: “Is not this written in the book of Jasher?” There is a book of Jasher, part of the Bible, one of the books Ezra wrote over, and we don't have it today.

Then 1 Kings: “Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Judah. Guess what? We don't have that book.

Rehoboam's acts were written down in full, and the Bible sends you to that book for the rest of them. The book is named, but it is not in our hands. It is another witness that more was written than what we hold today.

precepts.text: The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. We do not have that today either.
precepts.point: Is it that book you see they have out there on the Bible apps? Leave that alone. The books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having relations with women, or Esau being saved, that is made up to throw you off. The teacher stays with what the Lord gave us: Christ said that which ye have already, hold fast till I come. What is in these 80 books, we can get the kingdom with that.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
The southern kingdom had its chronicles, and so did the northern: “And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.” So there is a book called the chronicles of the kings of Israel, and we don't have that today either.

The book of Jasher is missing the same way. Is it that book of Jasher they have out there on the Bible apps? No. Those of y'all that have Bible apps, leave that book alone. It is said to contradict a lot of the Bible, and the books of all the prophets complement each other; they do not contradict each other. If you read a book talking about angels having sex with women, or Esau being saved, and all kind of wacky things, that is Esau making stuff up to throw you off.

There is a real book of Jasher, and the Pope and them likely have it in the Vatican, in those catacombs. But they put misinformation out there to try to confuse the prophets.

So the chronicles of the kings of Judah and of the kings of Israel, and the book of Jasher, are named in the scriptures but are not in our hands. What is out there under their names is not to be trusted.

precepts.text: Jeroboam made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back.
precepts.point: Therefore the Most High will bring evil on his house, cut off every male, and sweep away the remnant as a man sweeps away dung until it is gone.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

precepts.why:
This is the heart of the charge against Jeroboam: “But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back.”

The Most High exalted him from among the people, “made thee prince over my people Israel”, and rent the kingdom away from the house of David to give it to him. Yet he did not walk as David, “who kept my commandments”. He made other gods and molten images and cast the Most High behind his back.

Therefore the judgment: evil upon the house of Jeroboam, every male cut off, “him that pisseth against the wall”, and the remnant swept away “as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.”

precepts.text: There shall be no sodomite of the sons of Israel, for the Most High forbids it in the land.
precepts.point: They built high places, images, and groves on every hill, and there were also sodomites in the land, doing according to the abominations of the nations cast out before them.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

precepts.why:
The law is plain: “There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” The Most High forbids it in the land.

Yet under Rehoboam, “there were also sodomites in the land”. Judah did evil and provoked the Most High to jealousy above all their fathers, building high places, images and groves on every high hill, and doing according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel. The very thing the law said should not be among the sons of Israel was there.

precepts.text: The abominations Judah practiced were the very things the law commands Israel not to do.
precepts.point: They built high places, images, and groves on every hill, and there were also sodomites in the land, doing according to the abominations of the nations cast out before them.

note.label: 1 Kings 14: Judgment on Jeroboam and the Reign of Rehoboam

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.”

The abominations Judah practiced were the very things the law commands Israel not to do. When the scripture says there were sodomites in the land, and that they did “according to all the abominations of the nations which the Lord cast out before the children of Israel”, this is the abomination it means. The nations were cast out for these things, and Judah took them up.

precepts.text: The same judgment was spoken over Jeroboam, cutting off every male and taking away the remnant of his house like dung.
precepts.point: The phrase him that pisseth against the wall refers to the males, whom the Most High said he would cut off entirely.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
The same judgment was spoken over Jeroboam: “Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.”

The words “him that pisseth against the wall” mean the males. The Most High said he would cut them off entirely. Now Elijah speaks the same words over Ahab, because he “sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the Lord”: every male cut off, and his house made “like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat”, for the provocation by which he made Israel to sin.
